topics: Data residency (EU/US) and cross-border transfer restrictions
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sethi (Redwood SE), Ava Nguyen (Redwood SA), Cecilia Martinez (Head of Cloud), Thomas Greene (CISO), Ravi Patel (Sr. DevOps), Emily Carroll (Privacy Officer)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, im Jordan from Redwood, quick round of intros?
[00:08] Cecilia: hi Cecilia, head of cloud at Midland Trust, thomas is our ciso, ravi handles infra, emily's privacy.
[00:15] Thomas: yep, thanks for setting up. we booked this to talk data residency and whether we can put creds or pii in your hosted product or we'll need dedicated/private.
[01:05] Jordan: great. brief agenda. we'll ask a few qualification q's about regs, logs, retention; priya will walk through deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private); then discuss KMS, audit logs, and next steps.
[02:20] Priya: quick thing up front, what's your primary regulator / jurisdiction? are we talking primarily US (FDIC / OCC) or EU clients too?
[02:35] Cecilia: mostly US retail banking customers but we have an EU private banking arm — some customer data cannot leave EU. so data residency is big. also HIPAA-ish controls for some health-related payments — not typical but exists for a subset.
[03:10] Ravi: and our security team is strict about logs: no plaintext request logs leaving our environment, retention caps at 90 days, and some endpoints must have anonymized logs.
[03:28] Priya: understood. so three constraints: EU residency for certain datasets, HIPAA-like controls for a subset, and strict logging/retention policies.
[04:05] Ava: to map these to Redwood: Hosted API (our public cloud) is easiest and fastest but by default it's multi-tenant and logs may flow through our hosted control plane; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools + tenant isolation for request processing and configurable logging; Private (VPC/on-prem) is full control plane isolation, customer-managed network, and can be air-gapped for extreme cases.
[04:50] Thomas: can you confirm whether hosted keeps full request payloads in logs? we have to avoid storing any customer PII in logs.
[05:10] Priya: by default we capture traces and token-level telemetry for cost/latency, but we have options. we offer token redaction and configurable retention, and for Dedicated/Private customers you can disable request payload persistence entirely and route logs to your own SIEM via syslog/forwarding.
[05:45] Cecilia: how about KMS? we can't have managed keys from your cloud if data can't leave EU. we need customer-managed keys and also HSM option.
[06:10] Ava: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integrations. Dedicated supports KMS integration too but the key custody options depend on the deployment region; for strict EU residency we recommend Private in an EU region or on-prem.
[06:40] Ravi: what about model artifacts or cache? I've read about kv-cache or prefix caching — does that persist user data on disk?
[07:00] Priya: good q. cache is in-memory by default and not persisted to durable storage in Dedicated; in Private you control disk persistence policies. we can disable kv cache persistence entirely for compliance-sensitive workloads.
[07:35] Thomas: cross-border transfers — if a EU customer's request touches a model hosted in the US control plane, that's a problem. how does routing work? can you pin requests to region?
[08:00] Jordan: yes, traffic routing by policy — you can pin by region, and we support EU-only model endpoints. For hosted customers we have EU regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU; Private is best when you need full control and no cross-border egress.
[08:35] Emily: audit logs: we need cryptographically verifiable audit trails and long-term export to our archive (7 years for some records). does Redwood support tamper-evident exports?
[08:58] Ava: we provide detailed audit logs with user, request id, model version, and action types. For Private, you can route logs to your archive and we can provide export formats. we don't currently guarantee a cryptographic timestamp chain out-of-the-box, but we can work with SAs for integrations (eg. pushing logs to your wORM storage).
[09:40] Cecilia: ok. liability question — if a request with customer PII is processed in your hosted service, what's Redwood's policy on data retention and deletion? can we have contractual clauses?
[10:05] Jordan: we do have contractual options for enterprise — data deletion, retention limits, and SLAs. for customers with strict needs we recommend Dedicated or Private and we include contractual commitments around retention and deletion.
[10:45] Ravi: perf question — if we go Dedicated in EU, what's throughput and latency compared to hosted?
[11:05] Priya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput since you reserve GPU pools; latency is comparable to hosted for identical hardware. our kernel selection and batching runtime is the same; differences are mostly in tenancy and autoscale policies. we'll provide benchmark numbers as part of the pilot.
[12:00] Speaker 1: (murmur) can you show sample audit log fields?
[12:10] Priya: yes, example fields: request_id, timestamp, route, model_version, shard_id, user_id(hash), token_count, response_time. note: user_id is hashed by default for hosted but we can keep raw ids in Private if required.
[12:45] Thomas: hashing is ok but we need to ensure we can map hashes back to internal ids for audits — so we need a reversible pseudonymisation approach under our control.
[13:05] Ava: that's doable in Private: you control the mapping and keying material. for Dedicated we can discuss approaches with the security team.
[13:30] Cecilia: what about penetration tests and SOC 2 attestation? do you have certs?
[13:40] Jordan: we have SOC 2 Type II, working toward ISO, and we run regular pen-tests; i'll share the pack with Attestation and our pen tests.
[14:00] Emily: on HIPAA — for message contents that are health-related, can you provide BAAs?
[14:10] Jordan: yes, we have a BAA for enterprise customers and for Private deployment we can sign BAAs. Hosted customers might require more controls; we'll review scope.
[14:35] Ravi: network controls: can we ensure all egress stays inside our VPC for Private? and for Dedicated, can you support VPC peering?
[14:50] Priya: Private is deployed into your VPC with no outbound internet egress unless you configure it; Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options.
[15:20] Thomas: any limitations on model updates and version pinning for Dedicated/Private? we need guaranteed model immutability for a given deploy for audit.
[15:40] Ava: you can pin model versions and we support immutable deployments for audit purposes; rollout must be explicit via our console or API — we also provide hashes of the model artifacts in audit logs.
[16:15] Cecilia: curious about costs — Private on-prem will be expensive. how do teams typically stage migration? start hosted dev, then Dedicated pilot, then Private for regulated workloads?
[16:35] Jordan: exactly. many customers do dev on hosted, production on Dedicated, and subset on Private for the most regulated data. we can help you scope that hybrid strategy.
[17:05] Ravi: are there controls to redact PII before it's logged? e.g., regex-based redaction or token filters?
[17:20] Priya: yes, we have pre-processing hooks and redaction rules — can do regex, entity recognition-based redaction, and client-side preprocessing. For Private you can perform redaction inside your network before sending.
[17:50] Thomas: can we run a proof-of-concept with synthetic data and then a smoke test using real data in a dedicated EU region? timeline?
[18:05] Jordan: yes. recommended flow: 1) start with synthetic in hosted for functional checks, 2) provision Dedicated in EU for perf/security smoke test, 3) evaluate Private for full compliance. we can provision Dedicated pilot in 3-5 business days pending contract.
[18:40] Emily: retention policy on embeddings — we use embeddings in search, do you persist them? we need ability to TTL or rotate embeddings within 30 days for certain data classes.
[19:00] Priya: embeddings storage policies are configurable; we can clear embeddings on a TTL and for Private you manage the embedding store.
[19:25] Cecilia: what about legal e-discovery — do you provide easy exports for a given user session?
[19:40] Ava: yes, audit logs + raw request/response exports can be delivered for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has standard retention windows but enterprise options are available.
[20:10] (brief cross talk about internal procurement steps)
[21:00] Ravi: ok, technical ask — can we do HSM-backed keys with FIPS 140-2 module?
[21:12] Priya: HSM integration supported for Private; for Dedicated, depends on region and provider but we can integrate with cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM).
[21:40] Thomas: any redwood monitoring hooks that we can integrate into our SIEM for real-time alerts?
[21:52] Ava: yes, syslog and webhook integrations for alerts; we also provide tracing hooks and per-route metrics export.
[22:20] Cecilia: what if we need to ensure no model weights leave our network — for some regulated use-cases we cannot rely on vendor-run models.
[22:35] Jordan: Private on-prem supports self-hosting of model weights entirely inside your infra. we also support private model cataloging so you can deploy open models you control.
[23:10] Thomas: ok good. let's talk blockers: our procurement team will need SOC2, BAA language, indemnity clauses. security will need architecture diagram and network flow.
[23:35] Jordan: we'll send SOC2 and BAA templates, sample architecture diagram, and a short checklist for Dedicated vs Private.
[24:00] Cecilia: is there any visibility into token-level cost in Dedicated? we want per-route cost breakdown for chargeback to product teams.
[24:20] Priya: yes, our Console has per-route token and latency breakdowns, plus billing exports that integrate with your chargeback system.
[25:00] Ravi: during the pilot can we run a set of red-team prompts to test data leakage?
[25:14] Ava: absolutely, we recommend doing an eval suite that includes leakage tests. we'll share an eval harness.
[25:45] (pause)
[26:00] Thomas: ok what's the ask from us to get started?
[26:10] Jordan: three things: list of compliance controls and data classes, pilot scope (endpoints + volume), and decision owner for procurement.
[26:30] Cecilia: i'll gather a controls matrix and send to Jordan.
[27:00] Emily: timeline for deliverables?
[27:10] Jordan: i'll send SOC2/ISO pack within 48 hours, priya will follow up to schedule Dedicated provisioning, and we'll aim to start pilot by next week pending approvals.
[28:00] (short conversation about price ballpark, Jordan gives ranges)
[30:00] Priya: i'll also note config details: disable request persistence, enable BYOK, set log retention to 90 days, and route logs to customer SIEM.
[31:00] Ravi: do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning?
[31:10] Ava: yes SAML + SCIM supported for enterprise.
[31:45] Thomas: any gotchas around latency if we enable heavy redaction or local pre-processing?
[31:56] Priya: some extra latency for pre-processing but usually in the tens of ms; batching strategies help keep token-cost in check.
[32:20] Cecilia: ok we need an architecture deep-dive next week with your solutions architects and our infra team.
[32:35] Jordan: noted. priya will reach out with available times.
[33:10] (brief chatter on availability)
[34:00] Jordan: quick recap and next steps — send security pack, provision Dedicated pilot in EU, schedule arch deep-dive, customer to share controls matrix.
[34:20] Cecilia: sounds good. one more question — retention deletion certification: can you provide proof of deletion?
[34:35] Ava: we can provide deletion logs and confirmations; for Private we can implement customer-side deletion with signed attestations.
[35:05] Thomas: ok. last question: do you have references in financial services who did similar Private deployments?
[35:20] Jordan: yes, we can share references — i'll include 2-3 FS customers in the follow-up pack (redacted contact info where needed).
[36:00] Emily: thanks, that helps.
[36:10] (wrap up)
[36:30] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling.
[36:40] Cecilia: thanks, speak soon.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels and truncated words; some acronyms mis-transcribed (eg. HSM vs HMS), but overall medium quality.

End of transcript.

Recap (verbatim):
- Redwood recommended path: dev on Hosted -> pilot on Dedicated (EU) -> Private for regulated data.
- Key asks: SOC2/ISO docs, BAA template, architecture diagram, Dedicated trial (EU), list of compliance controls.
- Timeline: Redwood to send docs by 2026-04-03; pilot provisioning targeted 2026-04-07; customer to confirm controls by 2026-04-09.
